name: Schönberg im Stubaital
kurzbeschreibung: The gateway to the Stubaital – picturesque village at the valley entrance, offering views of the Stubaier Alpen and the ruins of the castle.
text:
Überblick

Schönberg im Stubaital is located in the Innsbruck-Land district on a panoramic mountain terrace at 1,013 metres above sea level at the confluence of the Ruetz and Sill rivers, home to around 1,100 residents. The village serves as the gateway to the Stubaital valley and a bridgehead to the Wipptal valley, situated just twelve kilometres south of Innsbruck. Schönberg features a well-preserved Tyrolean village ensemble with historic inns, providing sweeping views of the Stubai Alps, Mount Serles, and the Nordkette range. It is world-renowned for landmark engineering marvels including the Europa Bridge (Europabrücke) and the historic Stephansbrücke stone bridge.

Geschichte

Archaeological relics indicate that the Brenner pass route across this terrace dates back to the Bronze Age and the Roman Via Raetia. The community was first documented in 1180 as Schonberch, meaning beautiful mountain. For centuries, Schönberg prospered as a vital post and staging station along the alpine transit corridor, welcoming luminaries such as Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, and Andreas Hofer. Between 1748 and 1749, celebrated priest-architect Franz de Paula Penz erected the Rococo parish church of the Holy Cross, adorned with delicate stucco by Bartlme Gratl. Spanning the gorge below, the Stephansbrücke stone arch bridge was finished in 1845 as Austria's largest surviving stone bridge, while the 190-metre-high Europa Bridge was completed in 1963.

Anreise

Transport connections to Schönberg im Stubaital are seamless. Motorists reach the village via the Brennerautobahn A13 motorway, taking exit Stubaital/Schönberg right beside the southern bridgehead of the Europa Bridge. Alternatively, a toll-free scenic route leads from Innsbruck along the B182 Brenner road across the Stephansbrücke in fifteen minutes. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck main railway station. From Innsbruck station, the Stubaital bus (VVT route 590) runs every 15 to 30 minutes, reaching Schönberg in only twenty minutes. Hotel guests holding the Stubai Guest Card enjoy complimentary regional bus travel.

Tipps

An internationally acclaimed attraction is the Europa Bridge: adrenaline seekers experience bungee jumping from a height of 192 metres directly out of the bridge pier, while sightseers enjoy breathtaking views from the bridge viewing terrace and visit the Europa Chapel with its Karl Plattner frescoes. The historic wooden Wittingwarte observation tower, erected in 1890, provides panoramic vistas across Innsbruck and deep into the Stubaital. A scenic family walk ascends along the Gleins animal path to the sunny Gleinserhöfe farmsteads (1,412 m) beneath the Serles. Architecture enthusiasts should visit the 1845 Stephansbrücke stone bridge and the Rococo parish church.
